panels.figure_caption: Histopathological findings of acquired reactive perforating collagenosis. (A) Low-power view demonstrating epidermal hyperkeratosis, mild spongiosis, acanthosis, and focal ulceration. (B) Intermediate-power view showing focal ulceration associated with aggregates of intracorneal neutrophils and a mild inflammatory infiltrate within the superficial dermis. (C) High-power view highlighting transepidermal elimination of altered collagen fibers, with the arrow indicating a vertically oriented collagen bundle perforating through the epidermis.
in_text_mentions: ence of immune complex deposition. Histopathological analysis demonstrated epidermal hyperkeratosis, mild spongiosis, acanthosis, and focal ulceration. The ulcerated area is associated with aggregates of intracorneal neutrophils with the presence of vertically oriented collagen bundles perforating through the epidermis. The superficial dermis showed patchy, mild, chronic inflammatory infiltrates with scattered neutrophils. There was no evidence of vasculitis or features suggestive of an immune-mediated bullous disorder. In conclusion, it was consistent with perforating collagenosis (Figure 2).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Hematoxylin-eosin histology from a patient with acquired perforating dermatosis shows a keratin-filled epidermal invagination with rupture and transepidermal elimination, supporting reactive perforating collagenosis. B: Masson’s trichrome demonstrates blue-stained collagen being eliminated through the epidermal lesion, a characteristic histologic feature of reactive perforating collagenosis. C: Orcein staining demonstrates brown elastic fibers in the area of perforating elimination in the acquired perforating dermatosis specimen. The caption establishes elastic-fiber elimination but does not specifically support elastosis perforans serpiginosa, so the panel is attributed to the article’s reactive perforating collagenosis diagnosis.
